Example0162.label: Datalog reading of the game reachability (written for this report; the operator is monotone, T is its least fixpoint; the universal step is spelled with a negated escape relation)
Example0162.text:
T(x) :- Target(x).
T(x) :- Pa(x), E(x, y), T(y).             % player-A vertex with some successor in T
T(x) :- V(x), not Pa(x), not Escape(x).    % player-B vertex all of whose successors are in T
Escape(x) :- E(x, y), not T(y).

Example0163.label: Datalog reading of the greatest-fixpoint safe set (written for this report; complement formulation: T = V ∖ Unsafe)
Example0163.text:
Unsafe(x) :- Bad(x).
Unsafe(x) :- E(x, y), Unsafe(y).
T(x) :- V(x), not Unsafe(x).

Example1030.label: Datalog reading of the greatest-fixpoint integrity core (written for this report; complement formulation: Keep = Base ∖ Removed, a row is removed when a requirement points outside the kept rows of its shard)
Example1030.text:
Removed(id, s) :- Base(id, s), Req(id, ref), not Base(ref, s).
Removed(id, s) :- Base(id, s), Req(id, ref), Removed(ref, s).
Keep(id, s) :- Base(id, s), not Removed(id, s).

Example5006.label: Side 1, appended delta (legacy Example1042); side 2, prepended delta (legacy Example1058); written for this report
Example5006.text:
AccA(x, y) :- E(x, y).
AccA(x, z) :- AccA(x, y), E(y, z).

AccP(x, y) :- E(x, y).
AccP(x, z) :- E(x, y), AccP(y, z).

notes.Example2004: The canonical re-encoding of the legacy obstructed case; the query seed Root is pinned to {"root"} by the precondition.
notes.Example2011: Models insert-only re-evaluation restarted from the maintained view; Differential Dataflow/Materialize are the motivation, not the mechanism.
notes.Example4036: In an earlier (rate-matched) encoding this containment had a quantifier-free certificate; whether the compiled-sequence encoding needs a prophecy level has not been checked.
notes.Example5038: Replaces the legacy correctness case Example2032, whose bottom-up loop is the reference program of the check; both sides are OpenFGA algorithms (Check by top-down dispatch, ListObjects by reverse expansion).
notes.Example5039: Replaces the legacy correctness case Example2036 (its loop is side 1).
notes.Example5041: Replaces the legacy correctness case Example2024; its over-approximating RESTRICT check is the invalid twin Example5042.
notes.Example1081: Legacy raw_new TGD case (GPT-5.6); one representative of the specialisation-in-generalisation template (1083, 1085, 1087, 1089 are its siblings, not included).
notes.Example1088: Legacy raw_new TGD case (GPT-5.6): forward closure equals the transposed reverse resolution under inverse seed views and bridge-proof witnesses.
notes.Example1090: Legacy raw_new TGD case (GPT-5.6): a ternary mode-carrying state equals a binary projected frontier; exact only because every node has a mode (existential dependency).
notes.Example1091: Legacy raw_new TGD case (Claude Opus): every link has a midpoint (existential dependency); containment in a constraint-closed policy view.
notes.Example1093: Legacy raw_new TGD case (Claude Opus): the provenance cover is closed under propagation up to a re-projected coordinate (head-existential dependencies).
notes.Example1094: Legacy raw_new TGD case (Claude Opus): every peer pair has a relay (existential dependency); containment in an administratively closed distance view.
notes.Example3001: Legacy raw_new invalid TGD case (GPT): the second program demands a certificate on reviewed hops that the dependencies do not guarantee.
notes.Example3009: Legacy raw_new invalid TGD case (GPT): the second program demands a matching audit tuple per promotion.
notes.Example3014: Legacy raw_new invalid TGD case (GPT): the proof is checked on the resource coordinate instead of the auditor coordinate.
notes.Example5002: Kept after the duplicate review: the loop coincides with 5001 up to transposition and seeding, but it is the corpus's only Datafrog case (2039 was retired).
notes.Example0133: Kept after the duplicate review at Leo's decision: it is 0132 plus the union outputs and an implied conjunct, but Val's Part 1 review kept both and the all-paths program is a classic program in its own right.
notes.Example0001: Carries the kernel-checked certificate for this triple. The classic Example0160 stated the same triple and was removed as a duplicate of this case.
notes.Example0013: The refutable twin of Example0001: the same schema, precondition and command under the false postcondition T ⊆ E, refuted by the two-edge instance E = {(0, 1), (1, 2)}.
